title: Fresh-eyes review built into every task

message.text: Ready to dispatch. spawn_agent: role `task-mastermind`, name `fresh-eyes-review`, model `claude-opus-5-5`, effort `medium`, `bypassPermissions`. Brief: ai/2026-09-28/fresh-eyes-review/requirements.md. Prompt: "You own one task. Your brief is ai/2026-09-28/fresh-eyes-review/requirements.md, and your task log is task.jsonl beside it. Work in one worktree of your own. Land with a checklist of the owner's asks, each with its proof. Post progress on card 2026/09/28/fresh-eyes-review-built-into-every-task, two sentences at a time." In short: three sizes (none for a small CSS fix, a fresh Sonnet for code changes, a fresh Opus with screenshots and the four UX questions for anything new), and merge.mjs refuses a branch that needs a review and hasn't had one.
Taken: I own the fresh-eyes review. One worktree, two Sonnet minions (review.mjs + merge gate, then docs and skill lines), design goes to mastermind-servex-3 first.

Design sent up and two Sonnet minions are building in worktree fresh-eyes-review: one writes review.mjs and the merge gate, one writes the doc and the skill lines. Next I prove it on three landed tasks and show merge refusing an unreviewed branch.
For task-mastermind-fresh-eyes-review: your plan is approved as written. Edit merge.mjs in the main tree, not in a worktree branch, because it has never been committed.

Built and proved: review.mjs sizes a diff and spawns a fresh reviewer (three real reviews: none $0, light $0.30, full $0.51), and merge.mjs refused an unreviewed branch, then accepted it after review. Last fix before landing: merge.mjs must accept a file the branch adds that the main tree has only as an uncommitted copy.

Dogfood: a fresh Opus reviewed this task's own branch for $0.70 and found 4 real bugs (e.g. a fix verdict could still merge if findings were misnumbered). A fresh minion is fixing them and answering all 12 findings; then I merge.

Landed — reviewed: 10 fixed, 2 declined. Every task now gets a fresh-agent review sized by its diff, and merge.mjs refuses a branch that skips one; the changes are in your working tree for you to commit (report: ai/2026-09-28/fresh-eyes-review/).

I checked the landed review against your three new asks. (1) The mastermind decides: mostly there already. The size comes from the diff, lowering it needs a written why, and a "self-evident" line goes into the skill. (2) Feedback settled in turns: missing. (3) Tracking whether reviews are useful: missing.

Ready to dispatch #13: role `task-mastermind`, name `review-turns`, `claude-sonnet-5`, medium, `bypassPermissions`, brief ai/2026-09-28/review-turns/requirements.md, to start after collab-rounds lands. The turns go: the reviewer's findings, then the builder answers each one, then the reviewer accepts or holds each decline, then the mastermind rules. Every review gets a line on the collab scoreboard, so you can see per model how often a review changed the outcome and the dollars per useful review.

Taken: review-turns (part 2) — turning review.mjs's one-shot answer into four logged turns (findings → answers → reviewer replies → mastermind rulings), a usefulness score on the Collab scoreboard, and docs. collab-rounds isn't merged to michael/dev yet (still in flight under its own mastermind), so I've merged its branch into my own worktree to build on its Collab Phase objects.

For review-turns, deliverables 5 and 6 are added to your requirements.md. First, take screenshots from the worktree's own server, not monorepo.localhost, because new pages show as 404s. Second, accept `noted` for note-kind findings, and make every refusal name the unanswered finding by number. Together these caused a false fix, stale, re-review loop at about $1.30 a round.

Landed on michael/dev. review.mjs now runs a review as four logged turns (findings → answers → reviewer replies → mastermind rulings), scores each settled review onto the shared Collab scoreboard, and a live Reviews view sits on /framework/ext/Collab/ (6 real rows, 4 backfilled from history). This task's own review caught 5 real bugs along the way — including two that matched an owner-reported pattern from another task — all fixed. Full checklist and links in task.jsonl's landing line.
